title: ChaCha Remote Operator MCP — self-hosted governed remote operations
problem: ChaCha DEV needs a first-party, zero-license-cost remote operations route that remains governed even when a conversational interface lacks direct access to the user's runtime. The conversational interface must never become the operational source of truth or gain direct technical mutation authority.
goals: Provide a self-hosted MCP endpoint controlled by ChaCha DEV.
Prefer the proprietary Remote Operator route over quota-dependent third-party remote desktop or terminal connectors when policy and runtime health permit.
Expose the private MCP to compatible conversational clients without public ingress.
Allow a conversational client to hand off functional BUILD intents to the existing Direct Operator without executing technical commands itself.
Preserve Guardian, Sentinelle, Bastion, canonical STOP, CCR, Universal Materialization Gate, lifecycle, append-only evidence and zero automatic external spend.
Keep the transport, authentication, functional-intent handoff and machine-operation policies as separate governed layers.
Support future multi-target operation by capabilities and contracts rather than platform-version-specific logic.
non_goals: Do not expose an unrestricted root shell over the network.
Do not expose credentials, SSH private keys, tokens or secret stores through MCP tools.
Do not impersonate a Tailscale user or fabricate Tailscale identity headers.
Do not create a second Direct Operator or a second operational source of truth.
Do not let the MCP call central-orchestrator directly; functional intents must enter through the existing Direct Operator.
Do not grant the gateway technical decision, direct execution, direct mutation or production authority.
Do not bypass Guardian, Sentinelle, Bastion or canonical STOP.
Do not auto-purchase hosting, identity, tunnel or SaaS services.
Do not use Remote Desktop Commander as an automatic fallback for this route.

current_change.purpose: Expose the already-qualified localhost Streamable HTTP MCP through a private conversational-client tunnel and add a fail-closed functional-intent bridge to the existing Direct Operator.

acceptance_criteria: The existing Remote Operator MCP remains localhost-only and uses Streamable HTTP.
Conversational-client exposure uses an outbound private tunnel and never requires public ingress to the MCP.
The gateway exposes only named bounded tools; raw command execution remains disabled.
Functional intent handoff targets the single existing chacha-dev-direct-operator.service and forces channel BUILD.
The gateway submits user intent, project and an explicit idempotent client_request_id; it never supplies arbitrary argv, URLs or technical execution plans.
Direct Operator machine ingress uses a dedicated service identity and never fabricates Tailscale-User-Login.
Machine ingress is loopback-only, fail-closed, replay-protected, runtime-secret-backed and disabled until independently qualified.
The service identity may read only jobs it owns.
Canonical user STOP blocks new functional-intent submission; an unreadable STOP authority fails closed.
Guardian remains mandatory downstream before any governed mutation; Guardian stop remediation must be able to enter the orchestration path without a Guardian bypass.
The MCP gateway has no technical decision, direct execution, direct mutation or production permission.
Bastion and Sentinelle review network exposure and production activation respectively.
CCR, UMG and lifecycle remain mandatory before ACTIVE state.
ChatGPT or any other conversational client is never the operational source of truth.
Remote Desktop Commander is absent from the target PILOT path.
architecture_invariants: GitHub remains the source-code and CI authority.
ChaCha DEV on ChaChaVPS remains the runtime technical orchestrator and operational source of truth.
The conversational interface acts only as MOA, MOE and functional orchestrator.
MCP transport, exposure transport, authentication, Direct Operator ingress and machine-operation policy remain separate layers.
Producer and verifier responsibilities remain separated.
A future component cannot become ACTIVE outside CCR, UMG, Guardian, Sentinelle and lifecycle gates.
No network exposure is permitted before authentication and Bastion review are qualified.
Capabilities, contracts, schemas, manifests and feature flags are preferred to major-platform-version branching.
